task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 -- design the fix for ISS-0106. The scope is already decided and is NOT yours to reopen: read the section 'REVIEWER sign-off -- amendment (supersedes the version target above)' at the END of docs/migration/decisions/0005-pin-formatting-toolchain.md (appended this run, dated 2026-08-21T01:25:50Z -- do NOT act on the earlier 2026-08-19 sign-off above it, which the amendment supersedes on the version target). Its subsection 'Scope for the implementation (ordered; for CODE-DESIGNER)' is addressed to you directly and lists Parts A, B and C. Your design must cover exactly that scope -- no more, no less. A decision record binds absolutely under core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence; if you believe some part of it is wrong, report that in result.issues and STOP, do not design around it.

WRITE THE DESIGN to lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md. Design artefacts carry signatures, type shapes, behaviours and decisions -- NEVER implementation bodies. A multi-line Elixir function body in the document is an automatic FAIL at the Step 2b gate.

WHERE THE ACTUAL DESIGN WORK IS. Parts B and C are mechanical and need specification, not invention: B is `mix format` on four named files, C is applying one already-in-repo idiom (an explicit struct pattern match, the same one ISS-0046 merged into lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex) at fourteen named sites. For those two, your job is to make the target set exact and verifiable, not to design anything novel. **Part A item 3 -- the new `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex` -- is the only genuinely new code in this run and is where your design effort belongs.**

WHAT THAT TASK MUST DO, per the decision (re-read it there rather than trusting this paraphrase): parse `.tool-versions`, compare the pinned Elixir and OTP versions against `System.version()` and `:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)`, and on mismatch print a warning naming BOTH the expected and the running version. Four properties are load-bearing and each is a constraint the decision states explicitly:
  (i) it runs FIRST in the `letflow.check` alias, before any format diff an agent might misattribute;
  (ii) it prints on mismatch regardless of whether the later checks pass, and is NOT suppressible by any flag or environment variable;
  (iii) it NEVER changes any other check's exit code -- it must not fail the build, and must not be capable of making a failing build look passing;
  (iv) it degrades gracefully -- warns, never crashes -- if `.tool-versions` is absent, unreadable, or unparseable.

SPECIFIC DESIGN PROBLEMS YOU MUST RESOLVE EXPLICITLY, because getting any of them wrong produces a task that looks right and misbehaves:
  * **The OTP comparison is asymmetric and this is a real trap.** `.tool-versions` pins a full Erlang version (`erlang 29.0.5`) but `:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)` returns only the MAJOR release as a charlist (`'29'`). State exactly how the two are compared, what counts as a match, and why -- a naive equality check between `"29.0.5"` and `"29"` reports a permanent false mismatch on a correctly-pinned host, which would poison the warning's credibility immediately and is precisely the outcome (ii) makes expensive.
  * **The Elixir line's format carries an OTP suffix**: `elixir 1.20.3-otp-29`. Specify how the version and the `-otp-NN` suffix are separated, and whether the suffix participates in the OTP comparison, in agreement with the previous bullet.
  * **`.tool-versions` is a general asdf format**: it may carry lines for other tools, blank lines, and `#` comments. Specify the parse contract -- which lines are recognised, what happens to unrecognised ones, and what 'unparseable' means concretely for (iv).
  * **Where the file is looked up.** State the path resolution and why it is correct when Mix is invoked from the project root (which is the only supported case), and what happens otherwise.
  * **Exit code and output stream.** State exactly what the task returns and where it writes, such that (iii) is structurally guaranteed rather than merely intended. Note that a Mix alias step which raises WOULD abort the alias -- so 'never fails the build' is a property of the design, not an accident, and you must say what makes it true.
  * **Non-suppressibility (ii)** must be a property of the design, not a promise: say what makes it un-silenceable, given that `Mix.shell()` output can be redirected by a caller.

DO NOT design a fix for the separate finding recorded under the decision's 'One finding this decision does not fix' heading (three runs merging past a red format gate on 2026-08-20). ORCH has already filed that as ISS-0110 / GH#363 / queue task 177. It is out of scope here and adding it would be scope creep.

Also out of scope for you, listed so you do not design them and do not flag them as gaps: the issue-record bookkeeping the decision assigns to ORCH/DOC-UPDATER (superseding ISS-0106's wrong root-cause note, and the addendum to ISS-0046's UNCONFIRMED version attribution).
acceptance_criteria: AC1 -- The design document exists at lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md and covers Parts A, B and C of the decision's implementation-scope section, with each of the decision's seven Part-A items addressed by number -- including item 2, the deliberate mix.exs no-op, which must be stated as an explicit instruction NOT to change that line and why, since an implementer who 'tidies' it into agreement with the pin would lock this host out of compiling.
AC2 -- The exact post-change content of .tool-versions is stated verbatim, character for character.

AC3 -- letflow.check_toolchain is specified completely enough to implement without inference: module name, the Mix.Task behaviour it adopts, @shortdoc, the run/1 signature and its return value, the exact parse contract for .tool-versions (recognised lines, comments, blank lines, other tools' lines, unrecognised content), the exact comparison rule for Elixir AND the separate one for OTP, and the exact text shape of both the mismatch warning and the no-mismatch behaviour. The OTP major-vs-full-version asymmetry described in the task is resolved explicitly, with the reason stated.

AC4 -- Each of the four load-bearing properties (i)-(iv) is addressed by name, and for each the design states the MECHANISM that makes it true rather than asserting the property. In particular: what structurally prevents this task from altering another check's exit code, and what makes the warning non-suppressible.

AC5 -- The failure modes are enumerated with the exact behaviour for each: .tool-versions missing; present but empty; present with no elixir line; present with no erlang line; present but malformed on a recognised line; a version string that does not parse. Every one of these must warn and continue -- state the message shape for each, and confirm none of them can raise.

AC6 -- Part B names the four files exactly and states the verification that proves it complete (a command whose exit code settles it), rather than 'run mix format'. Part C names all fourteen sites by file:line, states the single idiom to apply, cites the in-repo precedent in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex that an implementer can copy the shape from, and states how the count is verified after the change. If your own count of the sites disagrees with fourteen, say so with evidence -- the number came from a measurement on this host and a disagreement is a finding, not an error to smooth over.
AC7 -- The document contains NO implementation bodies. Signatures, type shapes, message-text specifications and decisions only. This is checked on sight at Step 2b.
AC8 -- The design states, for the mix.exs alias change, the exact resulting alias list in order, so an implementer cannot place the new step anywhere but first.

AC9 -- The document states the ordering/independence relationship between Parts A, B and C explicitly (the decision records that B and C were never blocked on the sign-off), so the implementer knows what may proceed in any order and what may not.
AC10 -- No file outside lib/letflow/design/ and your own handoff is modified. You do not implement any part of this fix.

result.summary:
Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md, covering exactly the amendment's Parts A (7 items, by number), B (4 files) and C (14 sites) -- no more, no less. The decision record was treated as binding; nothing in it is designed around and no part of it is disputed.

MEASUREMENTS RE-DERIVED THIS STEP rather than inherited from step 01 (docs/anti-patterns.md, 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it'): M1 `mix format --check-formatted` -> exit 1, exactly the same 4 files with the same diffs; M2 `mix compile --force` -> exactly 14 'is expected on struct update' warnings and no other warning class, file:line trailers matching step 01's list exactly (no disagreement on the count of fourteen to report); M3 System.version() -> "1.20.3"; M4 :erlang.system_info(:otp_release) -> ~c"29" charlist, List.to_string/1 -> "29".

M5 IS A NEW MEASUREMENT NOT IN STEP 01 AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Because letflow.check_toolchain must live in lib/mix/tasks/ (Part A item 3), Mix has to load its module to run it, which forces a project compile as the FIRST thing `mix letflow.check` does (the task-discovery-forces-compile effect the existing mix.exs:49-55 comment describes). That raises a real hazard against property (iii): if the project is already compiled by the time `compile --warnings-as-errors` runs as step 3, does it find nothing to recompile and silently pass, turning a failing build into a passing one? Measured, not reasoned: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` with the project already fully compiled and nothing to recompile still exits 1 and re-emits all 14 warnings from the compile manifest. The warnings-as-errors gate is NOT weakened by the new first step. Recorded as M5, re-verified as V4/V5, and the mix.exs:49-55 comment is scheduled for an update saying so.

DESIGN CONTENT, the four things the task said were the real design problems:
(1) OTP asymmetry resolved explicitly (A3.5): compare the pinned erlang token's MAJOR component only -- substring before the first '.' -- against List.to_string(:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)), by exact binary equality. Reason stated in the document: otp_release only ever carries the major, so comparing "29.0.5" to "29" would report a permanent false mismatch on a correctly-pinned host, and because property (ii) makes the warning unsuppressible a false positive trains every reader to ignore the one message the whole mechanism consists of. The .0.5 is displayed in the warning ('expected 29 (from erlang 29.0.5)') but never compared. The consequent blind spot (OTP 29.0.1 vs a 29.0.5 pin is not detected) is documented as an accepted limitation with its reason and as OQ2, and the @moduledoc is required to state it so no later run 'fixes' it into a false mismatch.
(2) The -otp-NN suffix on `elixir 1.20.3-otp-29` is split off at the literal "-otp-" and DISCARDED -- it does not participate in the OTP comparison and is not compared to anything. Reason stated: it names the OTP major the asdf Elixir BUILD was compiled against, not the runtime; the erlang line is the authoritative OTP expectation; comparing both would yield two OTP verdicts with no precedence rule between them. Raised as OQ3 that this means an internally-inconsistent .tool-versions is not flagged.
(3) Parse contract is total (A3.3): CRLF stripped (a \r left on 29.0.5 would itself be a permanent false mismatch on these Windows hosts), '#' to end-of-line dropped, blank/comment-only lines skipped silently, whitespace-token split, only exact-lowercase 'elixir' and 'erlang' recognised, every other tool's line ignored SILENTLY, extra tokens ignored, first occurrence wins on duplicates, a recognised tool with no version token = no pin plus the raw line quoted. 'Unparseable' is defined concretely as 'the file could not be read at all'; once read there is no third parse-error outcome, because both comparisons are exact string equality on split strings with no numeric or Version parsing anywhere -- so 'elixir abc' degrades to an ordinary MISMATCH rather than an error.
(4) Path resolution: File.cwd/0 (non-raising, NOT File.cwd!/0) joined with '.tool-versions'; correct because Mix loads mix.exs from the cwd and does not search parents, so if a project is loaded at all the cwd is the root. Mix.Project.project_file/0 explicitly rejected because it raises Mix.NoProjectError. Non-root invocation degrades to failure mode F1.

PROPERTIES (i)-(iv) EACH GIVEN A MECHANISM, NOT AN ASSERTION (A3.6). (i) is a property of the alias DATA -- the task is the literal first list element, there is no ordering logic inside the task. (ii) rests on three structural facts: it runs before the other steps and never inspects them; output goes to :stderr via IO.puts(:stderr, ...) NOT Mix.shell(), specifically because Mix.shell() is globally replaceable (Mix.shell(Mix.Shell.Quiet)) and honours --quiet/MIX_QUIET while IO.puts(:stderr, ...) bypasses Mix's shell entirely and also survives a caller piping stdout into grep; and no suppression surface exists to use -- the task reads no env var and parses no switch, so non-suppressibility is an ABSENCE OF MECHANISM rather than a promise, with the implementer forbidden from adding one. (iii) rests on the fact that a Mix alias aborts only on a step that RAISES (return values are ignored), so the task cannot touch an exit code if it cannot raise: no Mix.raise/raise/throw/exit/System.halt/System.stop anywhere (grep-checkable, V8), every external call in a non-raising form, and the whole run/1 body additionally guarded so any unforeseen exception becomes failure mode F8 and :ok. It also cannot make a failing build look passing because it never wraps, invokes or intercepts another step -- plus M5 above closes the one non-obvious route by which it could have. (iv) rests on the parse being total plus non-raising APIs for the only two genuinely failing operations.

FAILURE MODES F1-F8 enumerated with exact message shapes and all returning :ok: missing (.enoent), empty/comments-only, no elixir line, no erlang line, malformed recognised line (raw line quoted), unreadable (non-enoent posix error), cwd unavailable, and any unforeseen exception. Two block titles are specified -- 'TOOLCHAIN OFF PIN' when a comparison was made and mismatched, 'TOOLCHAIN PIN NOT CHECKED' when no comparison could be made -- so a reader never confuses 'you are off pin' with 'I could not tell'. The mismatch block always prints BOTH the Elixir and OTP lines with expected and running versions on each, and must carry a verbatim 'This is a WARNING. It does NOT fail the build' sentence, because a loud block above a red gate is otherwise misattributed -- the same misattribution failure ISS-0106 was filed over. No-mismatch behaviour is one line to STDOUT confirming the check ran.

AC1's mix.exs no-op (item 2) is written as an explicit DO-NOT-EDIT instruction with the lock-out consequence spelled out (~> 1.18 = >= 1.18.0 and < 2.0.0; tightening to ~> 1.18.0 would stop the only confirmed-live host compiling at all) and a note that any future narrowing needs REVIEWER sign-off rather than a consistency cleanup.

AC8's alias list is given in full, in order, with letflow.check_toolchain first and the three existing entries unchanged.
AC9's ordering: B and C independent of A and of each other, in any order; within A, A3 -> A1 -> A4 must land together (A4 before A3 makes `mix letflow.check` fail with an unknown-task error; A3 before A1 warns falsely, since the file on disk today pins 1.18.3/OTP 27 which this host does not run); A5/A6 order-free; A7 is a no-op.
AC6's Part C table gives all 14 sites as update-site file:line:col AND the separate BIND site to annotate, taken from the compiler's own 'when defining the variable X, you must also pattern match on %S{}' remedy lines -- because for 12 of the 14 the edit does not go where the warning points. Precedent cited at lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:591 (a head binding both structs immediately above a %Token{token | ...} update), with the full ISS-0046 instance list. Verification for B and C is an exit code in both cases (mix format --check-formatted -> 0; mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors -> 0), never 'run mix format' or 'count to 14', and the design tells the implementer to report 14+N honestly if narrowing a type surfaces a previously masked site.

NO IMPLEMENTATION BODIES. The document contains signatures (@spec run([String.t()]) :: :ok), a module surface table, message-text specifications, file-content specifications, data literals that AC2/AC8 require verbatim (.tool-versions content, the alias list), quoted existing lines being replaced, and one cited existing function HEAD as the Part C precedent shape. No function body, no new .ex/.exs code block.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: ISS-0110's gate-discipline finding is named as out of scope with its GH#363/queue-177 attribution, and the ORCH/DOC-UPDATER issue-record bookkeeping is named as out of scope so it is not read as a gap. CI and warning-to-hard-failure promotion likewise.

No file outside lib/letflow/design/ and this handoff was modified (AC10). No part of the fix was implemented: .tool-versions, mix.exs, lib/mix/tasks/ and every engine file are untouched. The only side effect of my measurements is _build/ artefacts from `mix compile --force`, which is untracked. ORCH's uncommitted handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json and docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml were left alone per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 7.

issues.description: OQ1 -- alias-ordering side effect of Part A item 3's mandated file location. Because letflow.check_toolchain must live in lib/mix/tasks/, Mix must discover and load its module before it can run it, which forces a project compile as the first thing `mix letflow.check` does. Two consequences. (a) MEASURED HARMLESS: the later `compile --warnings-as-errors` step still exits 1 with all warnings re-emitted from the compile manifest even when nothing needs recompiling (M5, measured this step on this host with the project already fully compiled) -- so the warnings-as-errors gate is not weakened and property (iii) survives. Re-verify as V4/V5 after implementation rather than trusting this note. (b) NOT RESOLVED: if compilation fails outright, the toolchain warning may never print at all, which is a partial weakening of property (i) in exactly the case where knowing the running toolchain matters most. I did not design around this -- the amendment names the file path explicitly and a decision record binds absolutely, so relocating the check to somewhere that runs without compilation is outside this design's authority. Flagged for REVIEWER; if judged material it is a follow-on, not a change to this run's scope.

OQ2 -- accepted blind spot in the OTP comparison. Because the amendment names :erlang.system_info(:otp_release) as the API to compare against, and that API returns only the major release, a host running OTP 29.0.1 against a `erlang 29.0.5` pin is NOT warned. The full running OTP version is only obtainable by reading <:code.root_dir()>/releases/<rel>/OTP_VERSION from disk, which is absent in stripped installs and would reintroduce a filesystem failure path into a task that must never fail. Documented in the design and required in the task's @moduledoc so a later run does not 'fix' the comparison into a permanent false mismatch. Raised so REVIEWER sees it as a decision rather than an omission.

OQ3 -- the `-otp-NN` suffix on the elixir line is parsed off and discarded, never cross-checked against the erlang line's major. A .tool-versions carrying `elixir 1.20.3-otp-29` with `erlang 27.2` is internally inconsistent and this task will not say so. Deliberate: the amendment specifies two comparisons, not three, and a third verdict would have no defined precedence against the other two. Recorded rather than silently resolved.

The explanatory comment at mix.exs:49-55 becomes partly outdated once Part A item 4 lands: it argues that REQ-003's task-discovery-forces-compile problem does not apply to the letflow.check alias because the alias 'reads from mix.exs data, never from a compiled lib/ module'. After this change the alias's FIRST step is exactly such a module. The design schedules an update to that comment recording the new first step, the forced compile, and M5's measurement that the later warnings-as-errors step is not weakened by it. Noted here so it is not mistaken for scope creep at the Step 2b gate.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for WF-03 Step 2b (hard gate on this design), then to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation. For ELIXIR-DEV: Parts B and C are independent of Part A and of each other and may be done in any order; within Part A the order is item 3 (new task) -> item 1 (.tool-versions) -> item 4 (alias), and those three must land together in one commit. Item 2 is a deliberate DO-NOT-EDIT. Section 4 of the design carries the nine verification checks (V1-V9), all exit-code or grep based; V8/V9 are the greps that enforce properties (iii) and (ii) on the finished file and should be run as written.
